note: IP Anonymize stores its retention policy in config object ip_anon.settings: policy (0 preserve / 1 anonymize) and period_<table> integers in seconds (-1 = forever/never scrub). On hook_cron (and drush ip_anon:scrub) the IpAnonymize service overwrites the hostname column with '0' for rows older than requestTime - period. sessions is always covered; other tables come from hook_ip_anon_alter (dblog->watchdog, comment->comment_field_data, etc). Config route ip_anon.settings at /admin/config/people/ip_anon (perm administer site configuration). Drush: ip_anon:scrub, ip_anon:policy. Medium/hard cases read/write ip_anon.settings via drush and restore shipped defaults (policy 0, all period_* -1) on cleanup/reset.

evals.prompt: I installed the IP Anonymize (ip_anon) Drupal module but old IP addresses are not being removed. What is the main setting I must change to actually start anonymizing IPs, and at what admin path is it configured?
evals.expected_output: Set the Retention policy to Anonymize (ip_anon.settings policy = 1); by default policy is 0 (preserve), so nothing is scrubbed. Configure it at /admin/config/people/ip_anon (route ip_anon.settings, permission 'administer site configuration'). Scrubbing then runs on cron.

evals.prompt: In IP Anonymize, each table has a period_<table> retention value (e.g. period_sessions, period_watchdog). What units is it in, and what does a value of -1 mean?
evals.expected_output: The period is in seconds: IPs older than requestTime minus that many seconds are scrubbed on cron. A value of -1 (or any negative/non-numeric value) means keep forever / never scrub that table.

evals.prompt: Which Drush commands does the IP Anonymize module provide, and what does each do?
evals.expected_output: ip_anon:scrub scrubs IPs now according to the configured per-table retention (only when policy is enabled); ip_anon:policy prints the current retention policy as a table of each table's retention period (or 'Forever').

evals.prompt: On this site IP Anonymize is switched on. Inspect the live ip_anon configuration and state the retention period (in seconds) configured for the watchdog (dblog) table.
evals.expected_output: period_watchdog is 3600 seconds (1 hour), and policy is 1 (anonymize). Read from ip_anon.settings.

evals.prompt: IP Anonymize is configured on this site. From the live configuration, how long (in seconds) are IP addresses retained in the sessions table before being anonymized?
evals.expected_output: period_sessions is 86400 seconds (1 day). Read from ip_anon.settings; policy is 1.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, using the IP Anonymize module, enable IP anonymization and configure the sessions table so client IP addresses are retained for at most 1 hour (3600 seconds) before being scrubbed. Apply the change to the live configuration.

Configure IP Anonymize on this site so that IP anonymization is turned on and log (watchdog / dblog) IP addresses are kept for 7 days (604800 seconds) before being anonymized. Save it to the live site.
